title: Gordian distance and clasper surgery for links
summary: In 2000, Habiro introduced the notion of $C_k$-equivalence of knots and links. This geometric filtration is closely connected to finite type invariants, a class of invariants including Milnor's invariants. Shortly thereafter, Ohyama, Taniyama, and Yamada proved that $C_k$-equivalence, and by extension finite type invariants, say very little about the unknotting number by showing that any knot is at most one crossing change away from being $C_k$-trivial for any $k\in \mathbb{N}$.
